body: CTT: your parcel PT48210 is held for a missing €1.99 fee. Pay within 48h or it will be returned: ctt-entregas-pt.top/pagar

signals.why: CTT texts come from the company name, not from an ordinary mobile number.

signals.quote: Pay within 48h or it will be returned
signals.why: A short deadline with a threat of return is there to make you act without thinking.
The domain is “.top”, not “ctt.pt”. Having CTT’s name inside an address does not make it CTT’s.
A tiny fee is the bait: the aim is to capture your card details on the payment page.

subject: IRS refund available: €412.60
body: Dear taxpayer,
After reviewing your return we have calculated a refund of €412.60. To receive it, confirm your IBAN and card details in the form below.
https://financas-gov-pt.info/reembolso/confirmar
The request expires today at 23:59.

signals.why: The domain is “financas-gov-pt.info”. Portuguese government sites end in “.gov.pt”; this only imitates the look.

signals.quote: confirm your IBAN and card details
signals.why: To pay a refund, the IBAN already on file is enough. Card details are never needed to receive money.
Same fake domain as the sender. The https padlock only means the connection is encrypted, not that the site is trustworthy.
Refunds do not “expire” after a few hours. The rush is part of the scam.

subject: Final notice: access suspended
body: Your access to Segurança Social Direta will be suspended due to security inactivity.
To keep your access, enter your NISS and password at: seg-social-acesso.net/validar
If you do not do this within 24 hours, you will have to go to a counter in person.

signals.why: The official address is “seg-social.pt”. “seg-social-acesso.net” is a different domain that anyone can register.
No legitimate sender asks for your password by email. Whoever receives it takes over your account.
A fake login page. To sign in, type the official address into your browser instead of clicking.
The counter threat and the 24 hours push you to click before you check.

body: Good afternoon, sorry to bother you. I sent €85 to your number by mistake.
Could you send it back by MB WAY? You will get a code by SMS, just tell me the code so I can cancel it and get my money back. Thanks!

signals.why: Unknown number, no photo, no history. Nothing links this person to you.
The codes you get by SMS authorise operations on your account. Sharing them hands over the key.

signals.quote: so I can cancel it and get my money back
signals.why: It creates a moral duty and a false technical reason. A mistaken transfer is settled through the bank, not with codes.

body: Banco Meridional: we detected a suspicious purchase of €749.00. If it was not you, validate your card now at meridional-seguro.com/valida to avoid a block.

signals.why: Fake texts can land in the same conversation as real ones, so the sender name proves nothing.
A scare (“suspicious purchase”) and an immediate action. The bank blocks the card by itself; it does not need you to click.
The bank uses its usual domain, not one with “seguro” bolted on.

subject: Overdue bill – service cut-off
body: Dear customer,
We could not debit your October bill. Open the attached document to see the amount due and settle today to avoid the service being cut off.

signals.why: “LusoMóvel” is just display text; the real address belongs to “mail-clientes.biz”.
This is a program pretending to be a PDF. Bills are not executables.

signals.quote: settle today to avoid the service being cut off
signals.why: A cut-off threat with a one-day deadline. Real bills have clear due dates and prior warnings.

body: Hi mum, this is my new number, my phone fell in the water 😭
I need to pay a bill today and the bank won’t let me into the app. Can you transfer €640 for me? I’ll explain everything later, I can’t talk right now.

signals.why: A new number with nothing saved behind it. People who change number usually tell you another way before asking for money.
Asking for money in the very first conversation is the goal. Call the old number or another relative before paying.
They prevent a phone call, which is exactly the quickest way to expose the lie.

body: We could not deliver your parcel today. Reschedule delivery here: enc.pt-rastreio.cc/9Fq and confirm your address and card for fees.

signals.why: Odd domain ending in “.cc”. Real couriers ask for the tracking number on their own site, not through a generic link.

signals.quote: confirm your address and card for fees
signals.why: Rescheduling a delivery does not need a card. If you expect a parcel, go to the seller’s or courier’s site yourself.
It names no parcel you ordered from this courier; the message is generic because it went to thousands of people.

subject: Mailbox full – action required
body: Your mailbox has reached 98% of its capacity. New messages will be rejected within 12 hours.
Increase your quota for free by signing in here: suporte-correio.help/quota
IT Services

signals.why: An “administrator” who is not on your domain or your company’s.
Fake technical deadlines. When a mailbox fills up you find out when you try to send, or from a notice by the service itself.
A fake login page to steal your email password, which unlocks all your other accounts.
Signing in from a link in an email is the gesture scams are after.

subject: Your payment failed – update your card
body: Hello,
We could not charge your €11.99 subscription. Your account will be suspended on 31 October.
Update your payment details: https://streampt-faturacao.com/cartao

signals.why: A domain with “faturacao” added: it looks official, but the real service uses the brand’s main domain.
A card form on an alternative domain. If in doubt, open the service’s app directly.
Asking for card details by email is the whole point of the message.
A date with a threat. The real service usually retries and warns inside the app.

body: You have an unpaid toll of €3.40. Avoid a €120 fine: settle today at portagens-liquidar.top

signals.why: Generic name, with no licence plate or route. A real debt says what it is and when it happened.
A small amount plus a large fine is the classic combination for making people pay quickly.
A domain unrelated to any toll operator. Only pay through channels you already know.

subject: Congratulations! You won a €500 gift card
body: You were one of 3 customers drawn this month and you won a €500 gift card.
To receive it, just pay €2.50 postage at hipersol-sorteios.shop/premio. You have 30 minutes to claim.

signals.why: The domain is not the shop’s. Genuine prize draws do not use hyphenated “.shop” domains.
You never pay to receive a prize. The payment exists to harvest your card.
A real prize does not vanish in half an hour.

body: Hi, I saw your bike ad and want to buy it now. I’ll pay with the platform’s protected payment.
Send me your name, your card details and the confirmation code so I can put the money in your account: pagamento-seguro-anuncios.net/receber

signals.why: A fake page imitating the classifieds platform.

signals.quote: your card details and the confirmation code
signals.why: To receive money an IBAN is enough. Card details and codes are for taking money out, not putting it in.
Haste, and willingness to pay without haggling or seeing the bike: a common sign in these scams.

subject: I need a discreet favour
body: I’m in a meeting and can’t take calls. I need you to make a transfer of €4,800 to a new supplier today.
I’ll send the IBAN details shortly. Please don’t mention it to anyone else for now, I’ll explain later.

signals.why: The name is the director’s, but the domain only resembles the company’s (“acme-solucoes-pt.com” instead of “acme.pt”).
They make sure you cannot confirm by phone.

signals.quote: a transfer of €4,800 to a new supplier
signals.why: Money for an unknown supplier, outside the normal approval chain.

signals.quote: don’t mention it to anyone else
signals.why: The secrecy is so nobody questions the order. Normal payments are not secret.

subject: Your driving licence expires in 7 days
body: Your driving licence is about to expire. To avoid a fine, renew online at imt-cartas-online.org and pay the €34.50 fee.
We need a photo of your ID document and your card details.

signals.why: IMT uses government domains (“.pt”). “.org” with “online” is an imitation.
The fine is only a threat to speed up your decision.

signals.quote: a photo of your ID document and your card details
signals.why: An ID copy plus a card enables identity and payment fraud. A genuine service does not ask for both by email.

body: Hello! We are a marketing agency looking for remote workers: earn €150 a day liking videos, no experience needed.
To register, send us a photo of your ID card and your IBAN right now. Limited places for today!

signals.why: A foreign contact who has never met you and writes in generic wording.

signals.quote: a photo of your ID card and your IBAN
signals.why: Identity and account data for a “registration” with no contract or interview. They are used to open accounts and launder money in your name.
Manufactured scarcity. The €150 a day for liking videos is the bait.

body: CTT: parcel RB123456789PT is now available for collection at CTT Point Mercearia Nova (Rua das Flores, 12). Bring photo ID. Deadline: 7 working days. Details: ctt.pt/rastreio

signals.why: An alphanumeric sender with the company name, not an anonymous mobile number.
The domain is “ctt.pt” and the path is about tracking. You can still type the address yourself.
A real, long deadline with no threat. Nothing urgent or payment is asked of you.

subject: You have a new notification on the Portal das Finanças
body: We inform you that you have a new notification in your Electronic Mailbox.
To read it, go to the Portal das Finanças by typing the address into your browser and sign in with your usual credentials.
This message is automatic and must not be replied to.

signals.why: A government domain, “.gov.pt”, and the name of a portal that really exists.

signals.quote: typing the address into your browser
signals.why: There is no link to click: it tells you to go to the site yourself, which is exactly the safe habit.
It asks for no data in the email. The password is only used on the official page.

body: MB WAY: you paid €23.40 to Pastelaria Doce Rua on 28/10 at 15:12. If you do not recognise this operation, contact your bank.

signals.why: An operation notification as the service sends them, tied to your number.

signals.quote: If you do not recognise this operation, contact your bank.
signals.why: No codes or links are requested. It sends you to your bank through channels you already know.

signals.quote: you paid €23.40 to Pastelaria Doce Rua
signals.why: It has an exact amount, merchant and time. If you recognise this afternoon’s coffee, there is nothing to do.

body: Banco Meridional: code 483920 to confirm the payment of €59.90 at LOJAONLINE. Valid for 5 minutes. Never share it, not even with the bank. Don’t recognise it? Call 21 000 00 00.

signals.quote: Never share it, not even with the bank.
signals.why: The code is for you to enter, without giving it to anyone. The warning is good practice, not a request.
A short code validity is normal and asks nothing of you beyond confirming something you started yourself.
No links: just a number to call if it was not you. Ideally you use the number on the back of your card.

subject: Your October bill is now available
body: Hello, Marta.
Your October bill (€34.90) is now available in your Customer Area. Payment will be made by direct debit on 10 November.
You can view it at lusomovel.pt/cliente or in the LusoMóvel app.

signals.why: The domain is the same as the operator’s website and the message uses your first name.
It points to the customer area on the official domain, with no attachments or card forms.
It reports what is already agreed and asks for no new data.

subject: Your order #A-48213 has shipped
body: Good news! Order #A-48213 (2 books) left today and should arrive between Thursday and Friday.
CTT tracking number: RB987654321PT. You can follow it at fiodeprumo.pt/conta/encomendas.
Thank you for shopping at Fio de Prumo.

signals.why: The domain matches the shop where you actually bought.
It points to the shop’s account area on the shop’s domain. If you do not recognise the purchase, do not click and go to your account.
Concrete details of a purchase you can confirm. Fake messages are vague.

subject: Requested document: contributory status statement
body: In reply to the request you made today on Segurança Social Direta, your contributory status statement is attached.
Do not reply to this email.

signals.why: The official Segurança Social domain.
It is a genuine PDF and exactly the document you asked for minutes ago. An expected, consistent attachment is normal.

signals.quote: In reply to the request you made today
signals.why: The message answers something you did yourself and asks for nothing more.

subject: Beware of fake texts in the bank’s name
body: Fraudulent messages are circulating in the name of Banco Meridional asking for card details or codes.
The bank never asks for your PIN, password or confirmation codes by SMS, email or phone.
More security tips at meridional.pt/seguranca. If in doubt, call the number on the back of your card.

signals.why: The bank’s main domain, with no strange variations.

signals.quote: never asks for your PIN, password or confirmation codes
signals.why: The message says the opposite of what a scammer would: it teaches you to refuse requests.
A link to an information page on the bank’s domain, with no login.

body: Hey! I just sent you the MB WAY request for your €12.50 share of last night’s dinner 😄
Just accept it in the app, the notification should show up now. It was a great night, we have to do it again!

signals.why: A contact you have saved, with real context. The message fits a dinner you both remember.

signals.quote: Just accept it in the app
signals.why: There is no link: the request arrives through the MB WAY app, and you approve it there.
A small, realistic amount you can check against the dinner bill. Still, always confirm the name and amount in the app before accepting.

body: Hello, Pedro. Reminder: dental appointment tomorrow at 10:30 at Clínica Sorriso, Av. da Liberdade.
Reply 1 to confirm or 2 to cancel.

signals.why: A business account you have saved or dealt with before, and the appointment matches a booking you made.
The urgency is just the appointment date. No threat attached.

signals.quote: Reply 1 to confirm or 2 to cancel.
signals.why: You are only asked for a reply digit. Never personal data or payment.

body: SNS: you have an appointment booked at the Health Centre on 4/11 at 9:20. If you cannot attend, cancel on 800 24 24 24 or in the patient area.

signals.why: A notification of a booking you made, sent by a health service you use.

signals.quote: you have an appointment booked at the Health Centre on 4/11 at 9:20
signals.why: A concrete date and place, which you can check in your diary. Fakes avoid verifiable details.

signals.quote: cancel on 800 24 24 24 or in the patient area
signals.why: Two ways to act, without a link. If you want to cancel, open the portal yourself.

subject: Last early bird tickets – only until Friday
body: Hi! You subscribed to the CiberLisboa 2026 newsletter and we want to let you know: early bird tickets (€89) end Friday at 23:59.
Programme and purchase at ciberlisboa.pt/bilhetes. If you do not want more messages, use the unsubscribe link at the end of the email.

signals.why: The same domain as the event you signed up to.
It is marketing with a deadline, and it is pressure. But it is tied to a real price, not a threat or loss of access.
A link on the event’s domain, which you can verify. The unsubscribe option is also a good sign.

subject: October payslip
body: Hi all,
The October payslip is now available on the internal portal, under the “Documentos” tab.
Any questions, come and see us in room 2.04. Thanks, Catarina.

signals.why: Your company’s domain, sent to everyone, signed by someone you know.

signals.quote: on the internal portal, under the “Documentos” tab
signals.why: It tells you where to go without giving you a link, and with no attachment carrying sensitive data.

signals.quote: come and see us in room 2.04
signals.why: It directs questions to a real person and place, not to a form.

subject: Car insurance renewal – payment reference
body: Your car policy renews on 15 November. To pay by Multibanco or homebanking use:
Entity 21999 · Reference 123 456 789 · Amount €214.30
You can also change the payment method in the customer area, or call your branch.

signals.why: The same domain as your insurer’s website.
A Multibanco reference can only be used to pay, not to withdraw money. Check the amount against your policy.
The date comes from the policy you hold, not from a threat.

body: Luzoeste: you can submit your meter reading until 30/10 at luzoeste.pt/leitura or on 800 100 200. Without a reading, your next bill will be estimated.

signals.why: The electricity supplier you have a contract with.
A real deadline, and the consequence is merely an estimated bill, not a cut-off or fine.
The supplier’s domain, and the action (submitting a reading) asks for no passwords or card. A phone number is also given.

subject: New sign-in to your account
body: We detected a new sign-in: Lisbon, Chrome on Windows, today at 08:41.
If it was you, you do not need to do anything. If you do not recognise it, change your password at contas.correioluso.pt/seguranca. Typing the address into your browser is better than clicking.

signals.why: A subdomain of “correioluso.pt”, the domain of the email service you use.

signals.quote: Lisbon, Chrome on Windows, today at 08:41
signals.why: City, browser and time you can compare with what you did. It does not ask for your password.

signals.quote: If it was you, you do not need to do anything.
signals.why: The notice only asks for action if it was not you. Someone trying to trick you starts with haste.
